channel.title: The Awesome Ledger — awesome-testing
channel.description: New entries across the GitHub awesome ecosystem, diffed nightly.

item.title: Time-Provider — via awesome-testing
item.description: JavaScript/TypeScript clock and timer injection with deterministic runtimes, so time-dependent tests run instantly and identically every time.

item.title: 100x Engineer Skill — via awesome-testing
item.description: Skill and CLI that makes a coding agent state formal properties before building, checks them, and records second-model review evidence before the work can be called done.

item.title: wardenIQ — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source (MIT), self-hosted test intelligence: generates test cases from requirement documents with an LLM and checks the real code against them for coverage.

item.title: Selenia — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source (MIT) Python library that finds Selenium elements from plain-English descriptions with a 24 MB model that runs on CPU. No LLM or API key; it raises an error instead of guessing when no element, or two elements, fit.

item.title: Ghostframe Replay — via awesome-testing
item.description: A screenshot that replays its own steps: clicks, timings and notes are encoded in a strip of pixels at the bottom of a JPEG, then replayed in the browser, with no account. MIT.

item.title: Chromium Builds — via awesome-testing
item.description: Unofficial Chromium browser and Android WebView APKs for every milestone since 83, for x86_64 emulators and arm64 devices, to test a web page or a WebView app on a specific browser version. Open source (MIT or Apache-2.0).

item.title: Apex verify — via awesome-testing
item.description: Checks whether an AI coding agent's change does what was asked: a second model writes checks from the task without seeing the change, proves they fail on the old code, and gives a verdict with evidence. CLI and GitHub Action, Apache-2.0.

item.title: pdf-snapshot-testing — via awesome-testing
item.description: Visual snapshot testing library for PDFs on the JVM (Kotlin & Java / JUnit 5).

item.title: VibeRaven — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source CLI that checks Supabase migrations for missing RLS and grants, and replays two concurrent requests on a fresh PostgreSQL to reproduce a bug and confirm its fix.

item.title: Gitoza — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source desktop test and task management that stores tickets, wiki, cases, and runs as Markdown in Git.

item.title: EvalShift — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source CLI for regression testing LLM apps and agents before a model change: replays the same cases on two models and reports which outputs and tool calls regressed.

item.title: Deep Link Tester — via awesome-testing
item.description: Builds shell-safe adb and xcrun simctl commands and a QR code for testing Android and iOS deep links, and shows which intent filter in a pasted manifest catches a link.

item.title: Agentic Test Explorer — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source (MIT) AI exploratory testing framework: LangGraph persona agents drive a real browser through a deterministic Playwright engine, and every bug found becomes a reproducible Playwright spec. Can generate test missions from a GitHub pull request.

item.title: Playwright State Lens — via awesome-testing
item.description: Experimental Playwright helper showing selected browser-storage field changes and step screenshots in one local HTML report.

item.title: ChronoStack — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source CLI that moves time forward across a Docker Compose stack (Postgres, Redis and your services together, no code changes) to test trials, renewals, scheduled jobs and outages in virtual time, with scenarios, seeded simulated users and JUnit reports.

item.title: pytest-glow-report — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open source (MIT) pytest plugin that writes HTML and JSON reports and keeps run history in SQLite.

item.title: Mockatoo — via awesome-testing
item.description: Free hosted mock OAuth provider for Google, GitHub, Microsoft, Apple and four other providers, so E2E tests in Playwright, Cypress or CI can sign in without real accounts, CAPTCHAs or app registration.

item.title: sitelooper — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source (MIT) CLI that records a browser flow from plain-English steps with an LLM agent, then compiles it into a standalone Playwright spec that runs in CI with no model, and repairs the spec when the app changes.

item.title: ShipShape — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source (MIT) Claude Code plugin that turns a plain-language goal into Playwright browser tests, runs each scenario twice to flag flaky results, and writes an offline HTML report with recorded video.

item.title: atrezzo — via awesome-testing
item.description: Claude Code plugin that serves API mocks as deterministic projections of one seeded data set and checks the rendered DOM against a YAML scenario.

item.title: agentest — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source CLI that runs 130 deterministic checks on recorded OpenTelemetry GenAI traces, A2A agent cards and MCP tool lists, offline and without an LLM judge, and exports JUnit or SARIF for CI.

item.title: Momentic — via awesome-testing
item.description: End-to-end tests for web apps in Chromium and mobile apps on hosted iOS simulators and Android emulators, written as YAML that mixes preset steps with natural-language AI steps and run from a CLI locally or in CI. Includes Mo, an agent that explores a running app from a brief and reports findings with evidence.

item.title: judge-check — via awesome-testing
item.description: Checks whether an LLM judge can tell good output from bad by mixing planted decoys and known-good answers into its real inputs, then reporting how often the decoys pass. Zero dependencies, with an offline demo.

item.title: e2e — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source end-to-end testing framework for web and mobile apps, combining natural-language agent actions with locators and assertions.

item.title: coverage — via awesome-testing
item.description: GitHub Action that compares LCOV and Go coverage reports against the base branch and posts per-file changes as a sticky PR comment.

item.title: Bite — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source CLI that checks whether recent "fixed" commits are really guarded by tests: it takes each fix back out and runs the project's own tests to see if any fail. Free mode needs no API key.

item.title: test-inventory — via awesome-testing
item.description: Extract declared tests, states and skip reasons from JavaScript and TypeScript source without running the suite, and compare saved inventories between revisions.

item.title: Buggregator — via awesome-testing
item.description: Local debugging server with a mock server (OpenAPI import), HTTP request capture and a fake SMTP server whose API waits for an email and extracts one-time codes.

item.title: blastradius — via awesome-testing
item.description: Test impact analysis for JVM projects (Maven, Gradle, JUnit 5) that runs only the tests affected by a change, using class dependencies recorded by a Java agent.

item.title: appfuzz — via awesome-testing
item.description: Fuzzes WebAssembly apps against a simulated backend and reports crashes, injection, n+1 queries and data leaks, with an exit code for CI.

item.title: AnalyticsProof — via awesome-testing
item.description: Regression tests for analytics tracking: replays recorded website journeys and reports which step lost a dataLayer event or GA4 parameter. Has a free plan.

item.title: ScopeHaven — via awesome-testing
item.description: Runs an AI agent's tasks against a local copy of your app, as different users, and checks whether "done" matches what the app's records show. Node CLI and GitHub Action, Apache-2.0.

item.title: Cerulion — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source robot runtime that records each run and re-executes supported native recordings against new code, exiting 1 with the name of the topic that changed, so a recorded robot run becomes a CI regression test.

item.title: evalship — via awesome-testing
item.description: GitHub App that finds flaws in your LLM evals, says on every pull request which evals a change broke and why, and finds prompt and model changes that win beyond chance.

item.title: llmdrill — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source CLI that runs your app behind a local fake of the Anthropic and OpenAI APIs, injects outages (529/503 overloads, 429 with retry-after, hangs, cut streams) and grades its retries, backoff, timeouts and failover.

item.title: Replay QA — via awesome-testing
item.description: Autonomous QA agent for web apps built on Replay's time-travel runtime recording and analysis. It explores an app from its URL, writes and runs Playwright tests, and delivers a root-cause analysis for each failure, backed by evidence from the recorded execution. Free tier, no credit card.

item.title: GenClass — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source browser library that reports race conditions in a web app while they happen (stale responses written over newer data, duplicate submits, failure storms) with a small on-device model. Its local MCP server re-runs a page with responses delivered in different orders to find races and replays one order to prove a fix.

item.title: bareenv — via awesome-testing
item.description: Runs a command once per environment combination (unset, empty, invalid) and reports the ones that break.

item.title: Bifurc — via awesome-testing
item.description: Local-first API client, mock server and traffic proxy for macOS, Windows and Linux, with a CLI for CI.

item.title: mendwright — via awesome-testing
item.description: Self-healing selectors for Playwright and Selenium in Python. Repairs a broken selector from a saved fingerprint of the element, asks a model only when that isn't enough, checks the repair on the live page and can write it back into your code.

item.title: Brume — via awesome-testing
item.description: Copies a subset of a PostgreSQL database to a test environment, pseudonymizing personal data and keeping foreign keys valid.

item.title: ghostwire — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source Linux tool that mocks ping, TCP connections, UDP errors and DNS per target address, with delay, jitter, loss and faults controllable live through an HTTP API; no proxy to point your program at, no root needed under exec.

item.title: Persqo — via awesome-testing
item.description: Runs AI personas (different ages, devices and patience levels) through a live web app in a real browser and returns ranked issues with screenshots and severity, plus ready-to-paste fix prompts for your coding agent. 3 free test sessions, no card; paid plans from $59/month.

item.title: Bite — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source CLI that checks whether recent "fixed" commits are really guarded by tests: it takes each fix back out and runs the project's own tests to see if any fail. Free mode needs no API key.

item.title: Random IMEI Generator — via awesome-testing
item.description: Browser tool that generates 15-digit IMEI numbers with a valid Luhn check digit, exportable as text, JSON or CSV.

item.title: s3-test-server — via awesome-testing
item.description: S3-compatible server for tests that runs inside your Node.js test process or standalone via npx, and works with any SigV2/V4 client (AWS SDK v2/v3, AWS CLI, curl).

item.title: vibe-testing — via awesome-testing
item.description: Open-source MCP server and CLI that scans web app routes and forms, runs browser checks with Playwright, and produces HTML QA reports.

item.title: telegym — via awesome-testing
item.description: Load testing for Telegram bots: a drop-in Bot API mock plus a k6 extension that drives virtual users.

item.title: qarunbook — via awesome-testing
item.description: Free shared test runbook where testers record a pass or fail per platform with screenshots, and an issue marked fixed sends the check back for a retest.
